title: Bethel
lead: "House of God," a town north of Jerusalem where Abraham built an altar and Jacob dreamed of the stairway to heaven. It became a royal shrine of the northern kingdom with Jeroboam's golden calf, was condemned by Amos and Hosea, and was destroyed by Josiah (Genesis 28:19; 1 Kings 12:29; Amos 7:13; 2 Kings 23:15).

sections.b: Abraham camped between Bethel and Ai (Genesis 12:8). Jacob named the place after his dream (28:19) and returned to build an altar (35:1–15). The ark stood there for a time (Judges 20:26–27), and Samuel judged there on his yearly circuit (1 Samuel 7:16). Jeroboam made it one of two rival shrines to Jerusalem (1 Kings 12:28–33). Amos was told to leave it because it was "the king's sanctuary" (Amos 7:10–13), Hosea renamed it Beth-aven, "house of wickedness" (Hosea 4:15), and Josiah burned its altar (2 Kings 23:15).
